operations.description: Return the caller's own AutoDS identity, resolved from the authenticated bearer token. Use ONLY these fields: `id` (the stable AutoDS user id), `name`, and `email`. The upstream endpoint is named '/users/list/' but returns only the current user.
operations.notes: Resolves the current user only (not other users). The response is a single-element list with the caller's user record. Consume only `id`, `name`, and `email`. All other fields (account status, onboarding/feature flags, store ids, timestamps, etc.) are internal service attributes — do not rely on, reason about, or surface them; they may change without notice.

operations.summary: Get the current user's add-ons and credit balances.
operations.description: Return the caller's own subscription state: which add-ons the account holds, and the credit balances it can spend. Read-only, takes no parameters. Use it as the pre-flight check before anything that needs an entitlement or a credit balance, and as the first call when another tool answers `forbidden` — this one answers whatever the account's status is, so it can say *which* entitlement is missing.
operations.notes:
Resolves the caller only. Consume the three list fields below and ignore everything else.

`user_addons[]` — one entry per add-on the account holds or has held. `addon_type` is one of `orders_processor` (sourcing / Fulfilled-by-AutoDS), `product_hub` (TikTok Analytics and the product-finding hub), `virtual_assistants`, `mentorship`, `ugc`, `ols`. `status` is a numeric code: 1 = active, 2 = canceled, 3 = expired (an upstream build may render the name "active"/"canceled"/"expired" instead, so accept either form). An add-on counts as ACTIVE when an entry for it is present AND its `status` is neither 2 nor "canceled" — so `expired` still counts as active, and no entry at all means the account never held it. Do not infer activeness from `expires_at` or any other field in the entry.

`user_credits[]` — entries of `{amount_of_credits, credit_type}`. `credit_type` is a numeric code delivered as a STRING: "1" = auto-order credits (the balance a sourcing request spends), "2" = product-finder credits, "3" = AI-rewrite credits. An absent entry is NOT a confirmed zero: the auto-order entry is omitted both when the balance is zero and when the balance source did not answer in time, and the two are indistinguishable in the response — so read a missing "1" entry as "no spendable balance established", never as "zero, confirmed".

`user_packages[]` — plan context; its `status` reads the same way as an add-on's.

Everything else in the response (ids, timestamps, nested plan and add-on catalogue records, billing and payment fields) is an internal service attribute — do not rely on, reason about, or surface it; it may change without notice.

Two properties to plan around. (1) Answering this call reconciles the account against a separate balance source under a bounded wait, so its latency is less predictable than a plain read — usually well under a second, but a few seconds is within contract and is not a fault. Call it once and keep the answer for the rest of the task; it is not a tool to poll. (2) It is permitted for every account status, which is why it still answers when other tools return `forbidden` or refuse an entitlement-gated operation. That makes it the right first call for diagnosing "why can't I do X".
